title: Reflective presheaf presentation of a presentable infinity category
statement:
Use the infinity categories and nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U\prime$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the coherent functor and mapping-space conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means $\mathcal U$-small, and $\mathcal S$ denotes the infinity category of small spaces. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category. There exist a small infinity category $D$, its presheaf infinity category $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, and functors $L:\mathcal P\to\mathcal C$ and $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal P$ such that $i$ is fully faithful and there is a coherent mapping-space adjunction
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,i(c))$$
natural in $X\in\mathcal P$ and $c\in\mathcal C$. Its unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal P}\to iL$ and counit $\epsilon:Li\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}$ satisfy the triangle identities, and $\epsilon$ is a natural equivalence. The functor $L$ preserves all small colimits, and $L(\eta_X)$ is an equivalence for every $X$. For every $X\in\mathcal P$ and $c\in\mathcal C$, precomposition with the unit gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(iLX,ic)\xrightarrow{\ \eta_X^*\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,ic).$$

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, implication (1) to (5), printed pp. 457-460; Definition 5.2.7.2 (localization means fully faithful right adjoint) and Proposition 5.2.3.5. The unit, counit and displayed precomposition formula spell out the reflective adjunction Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Unpack presentability using [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Choose an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ and an essentially small full subcategory of $\kappa$-compact generators. Call this subcategory $A$, choose an equivalence $e:D\to A$ from a small quasicategory, and write $f:D\to\mathcal C$ for its composite with the full inclusion. If $q:I\to A$ presents an object, choose a quasi-inverse $r:A\to D$ and put $p=rq$; the equivalence $er\simeq\operatorname{id}_A$ identifies $fp$ with the original diagram in $\mathcal C$ and identifies their cocones, so the same colimit is obtained. Full faithfulness of the inclusion and of $e$ makes $f$ fully faithful, and its values are $\kappa$-compact because they lie in $A$. Thus every $c\in\mathcal C$ has a specified small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $c\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{a\in I}f(p(a))$ with $p:I\to D$. Here only a presentation of the particular object under consideration is chosen; the functors below are not defined by making unrelated choices of such presentations. The category $\mathcal C$ is locally small and has all small colimits, including the empty colimit.

source.place: Definition 5.5.0.1; accessibility convention of Proposition 5.4.2.2. Agent argument from compact generators, for the conclusion of Theorem 5.5.1.1(5).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ and $j(d)=\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. Construct $i$ by composing the coherent Yoneda functor of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] for $\mathcal C$ with restriction along $f^{\mathrm{op}}$. In particular $i(c)(d)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(d),c)$ is a small space, and full faithfulness of $f$ gives a coherent equivalence $if\simeq j$. Let $q:I\to\mathcal C$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram with a specified colimiting cocone to $c$. Fix $d\in D$ and write $H_d(a)=i(q(a))(d)$ and $M_d=i(c)(d)$, including their induced cocone. The current definition [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] says that this mapping-space cocone, viewed in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$, is colimiting: compactness is defined using the larger-space-valued coherent corepresented functor, not by presupposing a colimit in $\mathcal S=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. To descend it, use [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe]. It gives a small-space colimit $Q_d=\operatorname{colim}_I H_d$ and says that the fully faithful universe inclusion $\iota:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$ carries its cocone to a colimit cocone. The given cocone to $M_d$ induces a comparison $\alpha_d:Q_d\to M_d$. After inclusion both cocones are colimiting, so $\iota(\alpha_d)$ is an equivalence: their universal properties give an inverse map of cocones, and each composite is homotopic to the identity since the mapping space out of a colimiting cocone is contractible. This uses the cocone/initial-object clauses of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], with $\mathcal U'$ as the universe of spaces and a further ambient universe. Full faithfulness of $\iota$ lifts the inverse and its two inverse homotopies to the small mapping spaces, proving that $\alpha_d$ itself is an equivalence. Thus the canonical cocone $iq\to i(c)$ is objectwise colimiting in small spaces. The pointwise colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied with the small parameter $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, now shows that $i$ preserves these colimits. All colimits in $\mathcal P$ and in this conclusion retain the original $\mathcal U$-small meaning.

source.place: HTT Definition 5.3.4.5 (corepresented functor to larger spaces); Corollary 4.2.4.8 and the universe-change statement of lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe; Propositions 5.1.2.2 and 5.1.3.1. Explicit descent of the compactness cocone to small spaces.

proof.text:
Fix $c,c'\in\mathcal C$ and use a presentation $c\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{a\in I}f(p(a))$ from step 1. Step 2 gives $ic\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{a\in I}j(p(a))$. The colimit mapping-space test of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] in $\mathcal P$ and in $\mathcal C$, together with [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation], gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(ic,ic')\simeq\lim_{a\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(j(p(a)),ic')\simeq\lim_{a\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(p(a)),c')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,c').$$
This identifies the actual map induced by $i$ as an equivalence: at each $p(a)$, evaluation at its identity sends the transformation induced by $u:c\to c'$ to the composite $f(p(a))\to c\xrightarrow{u}c'$. These are exactly the components of the colimit comparison on the right, including their coherent compatibilities. Hence the map on the entire mapping space, rather than just on components, is inverted by the displayed chain. This proves full faithfulness of $i$. Every limit here is indexed by the small $I^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1(1) to (5), agent expansion via restricted Yoneda; Propositions 5.1.3.1-5.1.3.2 and Lemma 5.1.5.2 supply the mapping-space tests.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], $\mathcal P$ has small mapping spaces and all small colimits. Apply its restriction equivalence with target $\mathcal C$ to the functor $f$. This gives a coherent functor $L:\mathcal P\to\mathcal C$, preserving every small colimit, and a coherent natural equivalence $Lj\simeq f$. Thus the colimit-preservation assertion of the item already holds. This construction uses the full free-cocompletion equivalence, not the adjoint functor theorem for presentable categories.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.5.6; construction of the colimit extension of the compact-generator inclusion.

proof.text: For $c\in\mathcal C$ compare the contravariant space-valued functors $K_c(X)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)$ and $R_c(X)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,ic)$. They take small colimits to limits by step 4 and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. On $j(D)$ their restrictions are naturally equivalent: $K_c(jd)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(f(d),c)=ic(d)\simeq R_c(jd)$ by $Lj\simeq f$ and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation]. Since $\mathcal S$ has small limits by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], its opposite has small colimits. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] with target $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $K_c^{\mathrm{op}},R_c^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal P\to\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$. A quasi-inverse to its restriction equivalence lifts the equivalence just obtained, giving $K_c\simeq R_c$. This lift is coherent in $c$ as well as $X$: apply that same quasi-inverse to the diagram of restrictions parametrized by $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, and compose with its two inverse-functor equivalences. Postcomposition by a quasi-inverse is defined on diagrams and all their simplices, so the equivalence is one of mapping-space bifunctors. One may use an additional ambient universe for this parameter functor category without changing $D$, the spaces, or the meaning of small. No limit indexed by the large $\mathcal P$ or $\mathcal C$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 5.1.5.6 with opposite target; Propositions 5.1.3.1-5.1.3.2 and Lemma 5.1.5.2. Agent construction of the natural adjunction equivalence.

proof.text: Step 5 represents, for each $c$, the presheaf $X\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)$ by the actual object $ic$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] to obtain a coherent right adjoint $r$ and its representing mapping-space bifunctor equivalence. Composing that equivalence with step 5 gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(-,rc)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(-,ic)$, coherently in $c$. Full faithfulness of the Yoneda functor $j_{\mathcal P}:\mathcal P\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] ($\mathcal P$ has small mapping spaces by step 4) identifies this with a natural equivalence $r\simeq i$, as follows. The displayed equivalence is an equivalence edge $j_{\mathcal P}r\simeq j_{\mathcal P}i$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S))$. Let $\mathcal Y_0$ be the full subcategory on presheaves equivalent to some $j_{\mathcal P}(X)$; since a full subcategory contains every simplex whose vertices lie in it, this edge and its inverse witnesses lie in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal Y_0)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] the corestriction $J_0:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Y_0$ has a coherent quasi-inverse $K$ with $KJ_0\simeq1_{\mathcal P}$. Postcomposition with $K$ is a simplicial map of functor quasicategories and carries equivalence edges with their witnessing $2$-simplices to equivalence edges, so $r\simeq KJ_0r\simeq KJ_0i\simeq i$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal P)$, the outer equivalences being $KJ_0\simeq1_{\mathcal P}$ whiskered by $r$ and by $i$. Compose the adjunction equivalence with this identification to write the adjunction as $L\dashv i$. Its representing equivalence is the one in step 5, and the cited adjoint criterion supplies its unit $\eta$, counit $\epsilon$ and coherent triangle identities. Consequently its forward map sends $h:LX\to c$ to $i(h)\eta_X$, and its inverse sends $g:X\to ic$ to $\epsilon_c L(g)$: these follow by naturality from the images of the identity maps that define the unit and counit.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.4.2, Definition 5.2.2.7 and Proposition 5.2.2.8; unit and counit of the representing adjunction.

proof.text: For each $c,c'\in\mathcal C$, precomposition by $\epsilon_c:Lic\to c$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Lic,c')$. Indeed, under the adjunction its value at $h$ is $i(h\epsilon_c)\eta_{ic}\simeq i(h)$ by the triangle identity $i(\epsilon_c)\eta_{ic}\simeq1_{ic}$; the map $h\mapsto i(h)$ is an equivalence by step 3. Taking $c'=Lic$ supplies $t:c\to Lic$ with $t\epsilon_c\simeq1_{Lic}$. The two maps $\epsilon_ct$ and $1_c$ have homotopic images under precomposition by $\epsilon_c$; using the same equivalence with $c'=c$ yields $\epsilon_ct\simeq1_c$. Thus every counit component is an equivalence, with an explicit two-sided inverse. The counit is already a coherent transformation by step 6. Apply the vertexwise-equivalence clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] with $K=\mathcal C$, using $\mathcal U\prime$ as that clause's small universe and one further ambient universe. The parameter and target $\mathcal C$ fit in $\mathcal U\prime$; this application does not change the original meaning of small colimits or spaces. This makes $\epsilon$ a natural equivalence, as required.

source.place: Section 5.2.7, reflective adjunction; explicit inverse argument from steps 3 and 6.

proof.text:
The other triangle identity is $\epsilon_{LX}L(\eta_X)\simeq1_{LX}$. Since $\epsilon_{LX}$ is an equivalence by step 7, $L(\eta_X)$ is its inverse and is therefore an equivalence. Finally full faithfulness in step 3 and the adjunction in step 6 identify the composite
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(iLX,ic)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(LX,c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(X,ic)$$
with precomposition by $\eta_X$: a map $i(h)$ is sent to $i(h)\eta_X$, and every map on the left is so represented on its full mapping space. This is an equivalence and gives the displayed unit-precomposition assertion. Along with steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 this proves every clause of the item.

source.place: Definition 5.2.7.2 and the triangle identities; explicit unit-precomposition calculation.
